exposure: Mode of delivery: cesarean birth, spontaneous vaginal birth, operative vaginal birth
mode of delivery (cesarean birth, spontaneous vaginal birth, operative vaginal birth)
Genital hiatus size:  less than or equal to 2.5 cm, 3 cm, greater than or equal to 3.5 cm
cohort: 1528 women recruited from a community hospital 5 to 10 years after their first delivery
finding: Compared to spontaneous vaginal delivery, cesarean delivery was associated with a lower risk of SUI, OAB, and POP, while operative vaginal delivery was associated with a higher risk of AI and POP.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was associated with significantly lower hazard for stress urinary incontinence, overactive bladder, and pelvic organ prolapse, while operative vaginal delivery was associated with significantly higher hazard of anal incontinence and pelvic organ prolapse.
followup_time: Median follow-up of 5.1 years after enrollment
